items.title: Binance freezes about $3 billion of the $6.3 billion stolen in its hack
items.why: Update: Binance says it has frozen just under half of the funds taken after a DevOps engineer's laptop was compromised. It will cover customer losses; Chainalysis and TRM Labs link the theft to North Korea.
items.action: Give admin and engineering laptops your strongest protection: phishing-resistant MFA, endpoint protection, and no standing access to production or money-moving systems.

items.title: PHP2Shell flaws now confirmed exploited, including on firewalls
items.why: Researchers report successful attacks on the two PHP runtime flaws patched October 21, including 24 compromised firewalls, and CISA has added them to its exploited list. Any server running PHP, including WordPress hosts, is in scope.
items.action: Update PHP to 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 or 8.2.35 or later (or ask your host to), restart the web server, and check internet-facing devices for web shells.

items.title: Cisco firewall VPN flaw is being used to knock devices offline
items.why: Cisco patched an actively exploited bug in ASA and FTD firewalls that lets an outside attacker crash the device when the SSL VPN uses secondary authentication.
items.action: Update Cisco ASA or FTD firewalls to Cisco's fixed release for your version, and check every VPN tunnel group, including the default one, for secondary authentication.

items.title: Ivanti ships more fixes for exploited Connect Secure VPN flaws
items.why: On October 29 Ivanti released patches for the remaining flaws in a chain attackers used to get root on its VPN and steal Active Directory credentials.
items.action: Upgrade Ivanti Connect Secure to 22.8R2.6 or 25.1.1.3, then reset the passwords of accounts the VPN uses to reach Active Directory.

items.title: Polymarket users lose about $2.1 million through a compromised website add-on
items.why: Polymarket says a third-party provider was breached; Hudson Rock found wallet-draining code in a DebugBear performance script embedded on the site. Polymarket removed the code and says affected traders will be repaid.
items.action: List every third-party script on your website and checkout pages, remove ones you no longer use, and restrict the rest with a Content Security Policy.

items.title: 319 Chrome extensions caught rerouting web searches
items.why: Researchers found extensions posing as PDF converters, safe-search and AI tools, with 13.4 million installs, sending searches through servers that could redirect users to phishing pages.
items.action: Review the Chrome extensions on work computers, remove PDF, search or security add-ons nobody needs, then run a full antivirus scan.
